- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak or align with 30-day moving average.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend (e.g., +0.1 to +0.4), model underreacts; increase forecast by 1–3% to match sentiment shift.
- Model underestimates true price drops when sentiment is negative and recent prices are trending down; add 1–2% buffer to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 5 days show strong downward momentum (sentiment < -0.4), model often fails to reflect mean reversion; adjust downward by 1–3% from 10-day average.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0 to +0.3), model tends to overforecast; apply 1–2% downward correction unless accompanied by strong technical breakout signals.
